event.title: Aarohi & Rohan's Maharashtrian Wedding
event.summary: A warm, tradition-led Maharashtrian wedding for 300 guests in Pune, with a morning Muhurtham, a vegetarian regional feast, a floral mandap, and practical guest-comfort and weather plans within a ₹25 lakh estimate.

budget.rationale: A well-connected hall with ceremony space, seating, basic furniture, power backup, and accessible guest facilities.
A vegetarian Maharashtrian meal for 300 guests with service staff, drinking water, snacks, and traditional sweets.
A floral mandap, ceremony backdrop, entry welcome, and warm lighting with a reusable decor plan.
Coverage for the Muhurtham, family portraits, candid moments, and a concise edited highlight film.
A traditional welcome ensemble, ceremony microphones, and a sound check within venue rules.
Digital-first invitations with printed cards for elders and modest locally sourced guest favours.
Ceremony attire, family styling, and makeup with a trial appointment included.
Ritual materials, priest coordination, ceremony seating, and a family-approved Muhurtham sequence.
A reserve for guest-count variance, transport, first aid, drinking water, and day-of essentials.

timeline.task: Shortlist accessible venues and confirm ceremony, meal, power-backup, and sound-rule inclusions
Confirm the Muhurtham sequence and reserve the vegetarian catering scope
Book photography and videography coverage for ceremony and family portraits
Approve mandap design, floral quantities, lighting plan, and setup access
Send digital invitations and collect meal and accessibility requirements
Confirm final guest count, dietary needs, serving times, and vendor advances
Pack ritual materials and confirm attire trials, transport, and family arrival plan
Run venue walkthrough, sound check, guest welcome, Muhurtham, and meal service

vendors.what_to_book: A hall with a ceremony area, meal service space, accessible facilities, and a written power-backup plan.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Comfortable seated ceremony and meal flow for 300 guests.
questions_to_ask: What furniture, setup hours, cleaning, and power backup are included?
Are outside caterers and traditional sound performers permitted?
What is the cancellation and overtime policy?
red_flags: No written backup-power or rain plan
vendors.negotiation_tip: Request a single written package with setup access and essential furniture listed before discussing add-ons.

vendors.what_to_book: Vegetarian regional meal, snacks, drinking water, serving staff, and sweets approved by the family.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Meal service for 300 guests with a separately confirmed reserve quantity.
questions_to_ask: Can the tasting and final menu be attached to the agreement?
How are dietary restrictions and food safety handled?
What is the per-guest rate for confirmed extra portions?
red_flags: No written menu or service schedule
Unspecified service, transport, or overtime charges
vendors.negotiation_tip: Agree on a transparent per-guest rate and a written method for confirming the final count.

vendors.what_to_book: A ceremony mandap, floral backdrop, guest welcome details, and safe warm lighting.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Mandap for the ceremony area, entry welcome, and simple stage lighting.
questions_to_ask: Are flowers, structure, installation, and removal included?
What setup access and electrical requirements do you need?
Can reusable materials reduce the final cost?
vendors.negotiation_tip: Ask for a line-item quote and prioritize the mandap and ceremony backdrop over low-visibility extras.

vendors.what_to_book: Ceremony coverage, candid photography, family portraits, and an edited highlight film.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Coverage sized for the ceremony and meal period for 300 guests.
questions_to_ask: How many crew members and edited deliverables are included?
What are the delivery schedule and image-use terms?
Is ceremony audio captured separately?
red_flags: No sample deliverables or written delivery timeline
vendors.negotiation_tip: Specify a short essential-shot list and request one bundled quote for photography and video.

vendors.what_to_book: A traditional welcome ensemble, ceremony microphones, and sound support compliant with venue rules.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Scheduled welcome performance and clear microphone coverage for the ceremony.
questions_to_ask: Who supplies microphones, speakers, and a sound technician?
What volume and finish-time rules apply at the venue?
Is a sound check included?
red_flags: No backup microphone or power plan
Promises that conflict with venue or local sound restrictions
vendors.negotiation_tip: Bundle the sound check and ceremony microphones with the performance timing in writing.

vendors.what_to_book: Accessible digital invitations, limited printed invitations, and modest guest favours.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Digital invitation for all guests and printed copies for elders who request them.
questions_to_ask: Can the invitation include map, timing, and accessibility details?
What is the minimum order quantity for printed cards?
Can favours be delivered in batches before the event?
red_flags: Large non-refundable print quantities before family sign-off
vendors.negotiation_tip: Use a digital-first invitation and print only the number the family confirms.

vendors.what_to_book: Ceremony attire support, makeup and hair styling, and a scheduled trial.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Styling for the couple with agreed arrival times and a family-approved trial.
questions_to_ask: What products, assistants, and travel are included?
Can the trial and final look be documented?
What is the backup plan if the lead stylist is unavailable?
red_flags: No trial or unclear extra-person charges
vendors.negotiation_tip: Confirm a fixed call time, trial scope, and travel costs in the booking note.

vendors.what_to_book: Family-approved ceremony sequence, priest coordination, and ritual materials.
vendors.quantity_or_scope: Muhurtham ceremony for the couple, with timings confirmed by the family.
questions_to_ask: Which ritual items should the family provide?
How long is the ceremony and what setup is required?
Can the final sequence be reviewed with both families?
red_flags: Unclear ceremony timing or last-minute material requirements
Assuming customs without checking family preferences
vendors.negotiation_tip: Review the sequence and item checklist with both families before finalizing purchases.

ideas.title: Marigold Muhurtham Welcome
ideas.description: Use ivory textiles, marigold accents, and a clear welcome sign that guides elders toward comfortable seating.

ideas.title: Regional Vegetarian Feast
ideas.description: Build a family-approved Maharashtrian menu with seasonal vegetables, a traditional sweet, and clearly marked dietary options.

ideas.title: Reusable Ceremony Mandap
ideas.description: Make the mandap the visual focus and use reusable cloth and foliage details to control costs and reduce waste.

ideas.title: Traditional Welcome Moment
ideas.description: Schedule a short traditional music welcome before the ceremony, with a sound check and an agreed finish time.

ideas.title: Thoughtful Local Favour
ideas.description: Offer a small useful or locally made favour with a simple note, or let guests contribute to a family-selected cause.

risks: The January morning may be cool; prepare a warm waiting area and confirm the venue's indoor ceremony option.
Guest counts can change; confirm the catering reserve quantity and per-guest overage rate in writing.
Venue sound and setup rules may constrain performance timing; confirm permissions and finish times before booking.
Ceremony timing depends on family-approved Muhurtham details; keep a named family lead available for final coordination.
assumptions: The host has requested a Maharashtrian ceremony and a vegetarian meal; confirm any family-specific rituals and dietary needs.
The estimate assumes a Pune city venue and mid-range service choices; vendor quotes and taxes may change the total.
Digital invitations are the default, with printed copies prepared only for elders who prefer them.
A small guest-count buffer is planned, but the final guarantee and settlement terms must be agreed with vendors.
